tools.name: SparkLoop
tools.pricing: Free to join the Partner Network and Upscribe recommendation widget (SparkLoop takes a share of paid-recommendation earnings). Paying other newsletters to recommend you is a separate paid program.
tools.pricing_source: official site (sparkloop.app/pricing: Paid Recommendations, Partner Programs and Free Recommendations all listed as included free; referral programs are a $2,000/yr add-on) + SparkLoop help center
tools.best_for: Getting paid recommendations and buying cross-newsletter referrals
tools.verdict: The best-known newsletter recommendation network. Earning from recommendations is low-risk; paying for referrals only makes sense once you know what a subscriber is worth to you.

tools.name: Supascribe
tools.pricing: Free (2 basic embeds, first 1,000 views, first 100 new subscribers); Starter $9/mo, Growth $20/mo, Pro $249/mo (all billed yearly); paid plans add $2 per extra 10,000 views or 100 subscribers.
tools.pricing_source: official site (supascribe.com pricing section; yearly-billed prices shown)
tools.best_for: Writers with their own website who want on-brand Substack signup forms, popups and landing pages
tools.verdict: Fills a real gap: Substack's native embed is fixed-width and unstyled. Independent (not affiliated with Substack), and only useful if you drive traffic from a site you control.

tools.name: WriteStack
tools.pricing: Hobbyist $23.99/mo; Standard $32.99/mo; Enterprise $99.99/mo; every plan has a 7-day free trial. (Yearly prices aren't shown on its homepage.)
tools.pricing_source: official site (writestack.io homepage pricing section and writestack.io/llms.txt)
tools.best_for: Writers who live on Substack Notes and want batch scheduling, research and Notes-to-subscriber analytics
tools.verdict: The most complete Substack-only Notes suite: batch scheduling, voice-matched Note drafts, analytics on which Notes bring subscribers, a filtered notification inbox, and now an in-app writing coach (Quill) plus an MCP server so Claude or ChatGPT can draft and queue Notes. Pricey for a beginner, and publishing still runs through its browser extension acting in your logged-in session (you click Sync to send scheduled Notes).
tools.notes: Independent; not affiliated with Substack. Also offers free standalone tools (posting-time heatmap, Notes roast, Note generator).

tools.name: Narrareach
tools.pricing: Audience Builder $19.99/mo ($199/yr); Revenue Writer $39/mo ($390/yr); Full Agentic Mode $89/mo ($890/yr). Every plan starts with a 7-day free trial, no card required.
tools.best_for: Turning long-form posts into Notes and cross-posting to LinkedIn, X, Bluesky, Threads and Medium
tools.verdict: Good if distribution beyond Substack is your bottleneck. Hands Notes to Substack's native scheduler rather than posting from a stored session.

tools.name: StackBuddy
tools.pricing: Free plan (scheduling and creator network free forever); Pro $12.50/mo billed yearly or $15/mo month-to-month. Every account starts with 14 days of Pro, no card.
tools.pricing_source: official site (stackbuddy.io FAQ and pricing section) + stackbuddy.io/terms and /privacy; Chrome Web Store listing (offered by Patrick God)
tools.best_for: Batch-scheduling Notes into posting slots and finding other writers to cross-promote with
tools.verdict: A Notes scheduler with a free plan that keeps scheduling, and its Chrome extension hands each Note to Substack's own scheduler, so Notes publish from Substack's servers with your computer off. Pro adds voice-matching AI drafts, analytics and LinkedIn cross-posting. Small one-developer tool; the extension acts in your logged-in Substack session and syncs your existing Notes to StackBuddy's dashboard, so read its privacy page first.
tools.notes: Independent, not affiliated with Substack. Chrome needs to be open only while a Note syncs to Substack, not at publish time.

tools.name: StackSweller
tools.pricing: Pro $39/mo, or $25/mo billed yearly ($250/yr).
tools.best_for: A simple cloud queue for batch-scheduling Substack Notes
tools.verdict: Does one job (a Notes queue that runs with your laptop closed). Be aware it works by holding your Substack session, and Substack now schedules single Notes natively.

tools.name: SubflowAI
tools.pricing: Pro Monthly $9.97/mo; Pro 5-Year $69.97 one-time; Premium $99.97 (5 years, includes Connect to Claude/ChatGPT). Connect is a $30 one-time add-on on Pro plans. 5-day free trial, no card; 14-day money-back guarantee.
tools.pricing_source: official site (genaiunplugged.com/subflowai pricing section and FAQ); Chrome Web Store listing v3.11.0, updated Oct 2, 2026, 5.0 from 10 ratings
tools.best_for: Batch-scheduling a week or month of Notes cheaply, with a visual calendar and AI Note drafts from your articles
tools.verdict: The cheapest serious batch Notes scheduler we've found (the 5-year plan works out to about $1.17/mo), and Notes are queued on Substack's own scheduler so they publish with your laptop closed. It's a one-person product that works through your logged-in Substack session (the Claude/ChatGPT Connect feature uses Substack's unofficial API), and the AI-in-your-voice features are optional: edit anything it drafts before it goes out.
tools.notes: Made by Dheeraj Sharma (GenAI Unplugged); independent, not affiliated with Substack.

tools.name: Byline OS
tools.pricing: Starter free (CSV import, 30-day retention); Growth $19/mo; Scale $49/mo. 14-day trial. Currently in private beta.
tools.best_for: Paid-newsletter writers who want MRR, churn, cohort and revenue-per-post analytics
tools.verdict: Promising revenue-first analytics built specifically for Substack. It is a beta product; live sync uses your Substack session cookie and undocumented internal APIs, so the CSV-upload mode is the safer start.

tools.name: Google Analytics
tools.pricing: Free.
tools.best_for: Seeing where your Substack traffic comes from (Substack lets you add a GA measurement ID)
tools.verdict: Free and worth connecting on day one for referral sources. Overkill for most writers beyond the acquisition reports.

tools.name: Google Search Console
tools.pricing: Free.
tools.pricing_source: official site (Google Search Console Help: "a free service offered by Google")
tools.best_for: Seeing which Google searches bring readers to your Substack and whether your posts are indexed
tools.verdict: The only way to see the actual search queries that find your posts. Free, but Substack says Search Console verification becomes available as your publication grows, so newer publications may not see the option in settings yet.
tools.notes: Substack's SEO help article (updated Sep 14, 2026) says sitemaps and Google Search Console verification unlock as a publication grows.

tools.name: Subshack
tools.pricing: Free (Subshack 1.0), including a no-signup public profile audit.
tools.best_for: Finding out which Notes and posts actually bring subscribers, and auditing your profile
tools.verdict: A free, measurement-first browser extension (Chrome and Firefox) that never posts Notes or articles for you. Optional welcome-message sending is off unless you turn it on, with daily limits. New and small, so expect rough edges.

tools.name: Bitly
tools.pricing: Free (with ads; 5 links and 2 QR Codes a month); Core $10/mo (annual only, $120/yr); Growth $29/mo ($348/yr); Premium $199/mo ($2,388/yr).
tools.best_for: Tracking clicks on links you share to social, podcasts and print
tools.verdict: Handy for knowing which channel sends readers. The free tier is limited; many writers can get by with UTM tags plus Google Analytics.

tools.name: Plausible
tools.pricing: From $9/mo (Starter, 10k monthly pageviews); Growth $14/mo; Business $19/mo. Free trial.
tools.best_for: Privacy-friendly analytics for your own website or landing page
tools.verdict: Excellent lightweight analytics, but you can't install it on a substack.com publication. Use it on a personal site that funnels readers to Substack.

tools.name: StackStats
tools.pricing: 1-year license $39 (renew updates for $29/yr; the app keeps working if you don't); Lifetime $79 early-adopter price (listed down from $129). One-time payments, no subscription; 14-day refund.
tools.pricing_source: official site (stackstats.app pricing section and FAQ)
tools.best_for: Writers who want churn risk, cohort retention, superfan and growth-source analysis from their own Substack exports
tools.verdict: Digs far deeper than Substack's dashboard and keeps your subscriber data on your own computer (Mac or Windows). It's a new one-developer app: installers aren't code-signed yet, and the optional Auto-Sync (beta) logs in to Substack for you, so manual CSV exports are the cautious route.
tools.notes: Independent; not affiliated with Substack. A read-only live demo is on its site.

tools.name: Orbit
tools.pricing: $12/mo or $120/yr, included with a paid subscription to creator Rebecca Spitzer's Substack (What's Working Right Now on Substack). No free plan or trial.
tools.best_for: Writers growing through relationships who want to remember who they've talked to across Notes, comments and DMs
tools.verdict: A thoughtful relationship tracker for Substack that never writes or replies for you, and you can ask it questions from Claude or ChatGPT. It works through a Chrome extension running alongside your logged-in Substack session (DMs off by default), and there's no way to try it before paying.
tools.notes: Independent; not affiliated with Substack. Access comes via a paid subscription to the creator's Substack.

tools.name: Substack Insights
tools.pricing: Free for publications under 1,000 subscribers; $9.99 one-time above that. The pricing card lists Notes analytics and conversion stats under the paid tier.
tools.pricing_source: official site (substackinsights.com pricing section and FAQ)
tools.best_for: Writers who want a cheap, private look at their best posts, best publishing times and Notes engagement
tools.verdict: A simple, inexpensive Chrome side panel that ranks your posts and Notes and exports a CSV with ready-made AI prompts. Analysis runs in your browser using your logged-in Substack session; it only reads, never posts. Small and new (v1.0 on the Chrome Web Store).
tools.notes: Independent; its Chrome Web Store listing says it is not affiliated with Substack.

tools.name: NoteStack
tools.pricing: Starter $8/mo or $60/yr (capped scheduler: 7 new Notes/mo); Pro $12/mo or $99/yr (no caps, adds AI Ghostwriter and Post Coach). 7-day free trial.
tools.best_for: Notes-first writers who want subscriber-conversion rankings, best-time heatmaps and a scheduler in one extension
tools.verdict: A lot of Notes analytics for the price, with data kept in your browser. Be aware the scheduler auto-publishes through your logged-in Substack session, and the AI features send your Notes text to its server and Anthropic. Skip the Ghostwriter if your voice is the product.
tools.notes: Made by StackTree Labs; independent, not affiliated with Substack.

tools.name: NotesIQ
tools.pricing: $4.99 one-time for lifetime access (analytics, scheduler, competitor lookups); 7-day money-back guarantee.
tools.pricing_source: official site (notesiq.app pricing section and FAQ; matches its Chrome Web Store listing)
tools.best_for: Writers who want a cheap, one-time-payment Notes dashboard with a best-time heatmap and a weekly queue
tools.verdict: The cheapest Notes analytics extension we've found, and it keeps data in your browser with no account. Very new (v1.0.3, launched Sept 2026, no Chrome Web Store ratings yet) from a solo developer, and its price has already changed since launch, so treat it as an inexpensive experiment. Scheduling publishes through Substack's own composer in your logged-in session.
tools.notes: Independent; its site says it is not affiliated with Substack. Launch listings in Sept 2026 quoted $19 lifetime plus a $9/mo AI add-on; the current site and store listing say $4.99 lifetime.

tools.name: Typefully
tools.pricing: Free (10 posts/mo, 1 social set; Substack Notes included); Creator $99/yr (annual billing only); Business $18 per social set/mo billed yearly.
tools.pricing_source: official site (typefully.com/pricing, rendered page; Substack support per typefully.com/changelog/substack-notes and Typefully Help Center "Publish and Cross-Post to Substack Notes")
tools.best_for: X-first writers who also want to post to LinkedIn, Threads, Bluesky and Substack Notes
tools.verdict: A polished writing-first scheduler that now publishes and schedules Substack Notes on every plan, including free. It handles Notes only (no long-form posts, no video in Notes), and its paid analytics are for X, so it suits writers who start on X or LinkedIn more than Notes-first writers.

tools.name: Buffer
tools.pricing: Free (up to 3 channels, 10 scheduled posts per channel at a time); Essentials $5/channel/mo billed yearly ($6 monthly); Team $10/channel/mo billed yearly ($12 monthly).
tools.pricing_source: official site (buffer.com/pricing and its machine-readable buffer.com/pricing.md; Substack Notes support per buffer.com/substack)
tools.best_for: Scheduling Notes alongside every other social channel from one calendar
tools.verdict: Reliable and affordable, and its free plan includes Substack Notes scheduling. The best default if you post to several networks.

tools.name: Hypefury
tools.pricing: Flexible $6/mo for 1 channel (plus $6/mo per extra channel); Full $19/mo for all channels; 7-day free trial, no card. No free plan.
tools.pricing_source: official site (hypefury.com/pricing, including FAQ: "Hypefury no longer supports X")
tools.best_for: Scheduling and cross-posting to Bluesky, Threads, LinkedIn, Instagram and TikTok
tools.verdict: Hypefury no longer supports X, so it's now a scheduler for Bluesky, Threads, LinkedIn, Instagram and TikTok, with auto first comments (Autoplugs) and an engagement builder. Substack Notes isn't on its channel list, so pair it with Substack's own scheduler.

tools.name: Taplio
tools.pricing: Starter $39/mo; Growth $69/mo; Pro $199/mo; 7-day free trial.
tools.best_for: Writers growing a professional audience on LinkedIn
tools.verdict: Effective for LinkedIn but expensive. Only worth it if LinkedIn is a primary acquisition channel.

tools.name: Repurpose.io
tools.pricing: Starter $35/mo; Pro $79/mo ($790/yr); Agency $179/mo ($1,790/yr); free trial of 14 days or 10 published videos, whichever comes first.
tools.best_for: Automatically distributing video and podcast clips across platforms
tools.verdict: Saves real time if you make video or audio. Pure text writers don't need it.

tools.name: Canva
tools.pricing: Free; Pro US$144/yr for one person (before tax).
tools.best_for: Header images, social graphics, Notes images and simple brand kits
tools.verdict: The default design tool for newsletter writers. The free plan covers most needs.
tools.notes: Affiliate: Canva Help Center page 'Become a Canva affiliate through the Canvassador Program'.

tools.name: Figma
tools.pricing: Free Starter; Professional full seat $16/mo.
tools.best_for: Custom visual systems, templates and detailed design work
tools.verdict: More power than most writers need. Pick it if you already know it or want pixel-level control.

tools.name: Kittl
tools.pricing: Free plan (personal use only); Pro $15/mo or $144/yr; Expert $35/mo or $312/yr; Max $65/mo or $576/yr (USD).
tools.pricing_source: official site (kittl.com/pricing plan data and FAQ)
tools.best_for: Typography-heavy graphics and AI-assisted illustrations
tools.verdict: A stylish Canva alternative with great type tools. The free plan is for personal use only; Pro adds a commercial license.

tools.name: Unsplash
tools.pricing: Free to use under the Unsplash License (commercial use allowed, no attribution required). Optional paid Unsplash+ subscription for exclusive images under a separate license.
tools.best_for: Free, high-quality photos for post headers
tools.verdict: The go-to free photo library. Popular images show up everywhere, so crop or edit them to stand out. Credit the photographer anyway: it's appreciated, though not required.
tools.notes: The license doesn't allow selling images without significant modification. Unsplash+ images have their own license (for example, no use in AI or machine-learning training).

tools.name: Excalidraw
tools.pricing: Free and open source (MIT license); optional Excalidraw+ at $6/user/mo with a 14-day free trial.
tools.best_for: Quick hand-drawn-style diagrams and process sketches to drop into posts
tools.verdict: The fastest way to turn a paragraph of explanation into a simple diagram: draw boxes and arrows, export a PNG, and add it to your post like any image. The free web app saves drawings in your browser's storage, which can be cleared, so save a file of anything you'll want to edit later.
tools.notes: Exports PNG, SVG and an open .excalidraw file. For Substack, add the exported PNG to your post as an image.

tools.name: remove.bg
tools.pricing: Free preview-size downloads (up to 0.25 megapixels) on remove.bg; full-resolution cutouts cost 1 credit each. Subscriptions from $9/mo for 40 credits ($8.10/mo billed yearly), or pay-as-you-go credits.
tools.pricing_source: official site (remove.bg/pricing plan data and FAQ)
tools.best_for: One-click background removal for headshots and product images
tools.verdict: Fast and accurate, and the free preview size is often enough for a small inline image. Now a Canva brand, and Canva Pro includes a background remover, so you may not need both.

tools.name: Grammarly
tools.pricing: Free (includes 100 AI prompts/mo); Pro from $12/mo with a free trial (2,000 AI prompts/mo, full-sentence rewrites, tone adjustments, plagiarism and AI-text detection).
tools.best_for: Catching typos and clarity issues everywhere you write, including the Substack editor
tools.verdict: The free browser extension is worth installing. Pro's rewrites can flatten your voice, so accept suggestions selectively.

tools.name: Hemingway Editor
tools.pricing: Free web editor; Editor Plus (AI rewrites) Individual 5K $8.33/mo billed annually ($100/yr) or Individual 10K $12.50/mo billed annually ($150/yr); desktop app $19.99 one-time (no AI features).
tools.pricing_source: official site (hemingwayapp.com/hemingway-editor-plus and /desktop; the old /pricing page now returns 404)
tools.best_for: Making dense posts easier to read
tools.verdict: The free web version does the core job (highlighting long and passive sentences). Most writers don't need Plus.

tools.name: ProWritingAid
tools.pricing: Free (500 words at a time, 2 runs per report a day, 10 Rephrases a day); Premium $10/mo billed yearly ($120) or $30/mo monthly; Premium Pro $12/mo billed yearly ($144) or $36/mo monthly. Lifetime options and a 3-day money-back guarantee on yearly and lifetime plans.
tools.best_for: Deep style reports for long-form and fiction writers
tools.verdict: More thorough reports than Grammarly. Worth trying if you write long essays or serialized fiction.

tools.name: LanguageTool
tools.pricing: Free (up to 2,000 characters per text field); Premium $24.90/mo monthly, $49.90/quarter, $69.90/yr or $119.80 for 2 years.
tools.pricing_source: official site (languagetool.org/premium, rendered page, USD incl. VAT)
tools.best_for: Multilingual writers and anyone who wants a Grammarly alternative
tools.verdict: Strong grammar checking across many languages, and much cheaper per year than monthly billing.

tools.name: QuillBot
tools.pricing: Free (paraphrase up to 125 words at a time, 2 modes); Premium $19.95 monthly, $39.95 every 3 months, or $99.95/yr ($8.33/mo). Prices may vary by region.
tools.pricing_source: official site (quillbot.com Premium page and QuillBot FAQ "How much is QuillBot Premium?") + QuillBot help center (prices vary by region)
tools.best_for: Paraphrasing, summarizing and quick rewrites
tools.verdict: Useful for tightening a stubborn paragraph. Don't lean on it for whole posts, because readers subscribe for your voice.

tools.name: Notion
tools.pricing: Free; Plus $10/seat/mo.
tools.best_for: Editorial calendars, idea banks and sponsor CRMs
tools.verdict: The most flexible planning hub for newsletter writers. The free plan covers solo use.

tools.name: Trello
tools.pricing: Free (up to 10 collaborators); Standard $5/user/mo billed annually.
tools.pricing_source: official site (trello.com/pricing; Standard is $6/user/mo billed monthly)
tools.best_for: A simple kanban for drafts moving from idea to published
tools.verdict: Simpler than Notion if you only need a board. Free is plenty for one writer.

tools.name: Obsidian
tools.pricing: Free; optional Sync $4/mo and Publish $8/mo (billed annually).
tools.best_for: Building a personal knowledge base of notes, quotes and ideas
tools.verdict: Great for writers who think in linked notes. Your files stay local in Markdown.

tools.name: Persistwise
tools.pricing: Keep plan: 30 days free (no card), then $40/yr.
tools.pricing_source: official site (persistwise.com) + maker's launch post (blog.ninepointlabs.com/2026/10/persistwise-launch/, Oct 26, 2026)
tools.best_for: Keeping an independent backup of every post you publish on Substack
tools.verdict: Set-and-forget insurance for your archive: give it your Substack RSS feed and every new post gets a public Wayback Machine snapshot, a pinned IPFS copy and a private copy it stores. Brand new (launched Oct 26, 2026) and honest about its limits: each post is captured once, so later edits aren't saved, copies are HTML without images, and there's no export button yet. Keep using Substack's own export for a full backup.
tools.notes: Made by Nine Point Labs; independent, not affiliated with Substack. Wayback and IPFS copies are public, so only add feeds for writing you're happy to keep public.

tools.name: newsletterapi
tools.pricing: Free (1 publication, recent posts from your public feed, limited API/MCP calls); Writer $9/mo (full archive from your export, MCP archive search, automatic backups); Pro $29/mo; Agency/Developer $79/mo. Priced per publication.
tools.pricing_source: official site (newsletterapi.io and newsletterapi.io/pricing; "You are never charged without confirming by email first")
tools.best_for: Letting Claude or ChatGPT search your whole Substack archive, and backing up every post with images to your own storage
tools.verdict: A read-only API and MCP server built from your public RSS feed and the export you download yourself: no password, session cookie or browser extension. The Writer plan adds full-archive search for AI assistants and automatic Markdown/HTML backups (with images) to GitHub, Google Drive, Dropbox or S3. It's new and run by an unnamed independent team, and access is set up by email invite rather than instant signup, so try the free tier first.
tools.notes: Independent; not affiliated with Substack. Read-only by design: it can't publish posts or Notes.

tools.name: Readwise
tools.pricing: Full Readwise (Reader + Highlights) $9.99/mo billed yearly; Highlights only or Reader only $7.99/mo; Highlights Lite $5.59/mo billed yearly. Free for the first 30 days.
tools.best_for: Collecting highlights from books and articles to feed your writing
tools.verdict: A strong research engine for essayists and curators. Its Reader app is included with Full.

tools.name: Google Trends
tools.pricing: Free.
tools.best_for: Checking whether a topic is rising before you write about it
tools.verdict: A quick, free sanity check for timely topics and post titles.

tools.name: Zapier
tools.pricing: Free (100 tasks/mo, two-step Zaps); Professional from $19.99/mo; Team from $69/mo.
tools.best_for: Automating busywork such as logging new posts to a spreadsheet or sending sponsor reminders
tools.verdict: Powerful glue between apps. Substack has no official public API, so automations usually start from its RSS feed or email.

tools.name: ChatGPT
tools.pricing: Free; Go $8/mo (may include ads); Plus $20/mo; Pro from $100/mo. Monthly billing only for individual plans.
tools.pricing_source: chatgpt.com/pricing (plans and features; individual plans billed monthly) + OpenAI Help Center (Plus $20/mo) + OpenAI Go launch post (US $8/mo)
tools.best_for: Brainstorming angles, outlines, headlines and research summaries
tools.verdict: A versatile thinking partner. Use it for ideas and edits rather than finished prose your readers will recognize as generic.

tools.name: Claude
tools.pricing: Free; Pro $20/mo or $17/mo billed annually.
tools.pricing_source: claude.com/pricing (Pro: $17/mo with annual billing, $200 billed up front; $20 billed monthly; Max from $100/mo)
tools.best_for: Long-document feedback, structural edits and drafting help
tools.verdict: Particularly good at critiquing long drafts. The same caution about voice applies.

tools.name: Perplexity
tools.pricing: Free; Pro $20/mo, or $17/mo billed annually ($200/yr); Max $200/mo or $167/mo billed annually.
tools.pricing_source: perplexity.ai/hub/pricing and /pro (annual prices) + Perplexity Help Center (monthly and yearly prices)
tools.best_for: Quick research with cited sources
tools.verdict: Faster than a search engine for background research. Always click through and verify the citations.

tools.name: Sudowrite
tools.pricing: Hobby & Student $10/mo; Professional $22/mo; Max $44/mo (credit-based; yearly billing advertised as up to 50% off). Free trial, no credit card.
tools.pricing_source: official site (sudowrite.com/pricing; Max plan lists unused credits rolling over for 12 months)
tools.best_for: Fiction writers publishing serialized stories
tools.verdict: Purpose-built for fiction, with tools for matching your style and keeping continuity across a series. Not the right tool for essays or news-style newsletters.

tools.name: Descript
tools.pricing: Free; Hobbyist $16/mo billed annually ($24 monthly); Creator $24/mo annually ($35 monthly); Business $50/mo annually ($65 monthly).
tools.best_for: Editing podcast and video by editing the transcript
tools.verdict: The easiest way for writers to edit audio and video. A natural fit for Substack podcasts.

tools.name: ElevenLabs
tools.pricing: Free (10k credits/mo); Starter $6/mo; Creator $22/mo; higher tiers available.
tools.best_for: Producing audio versions of posts with natural-sounding AI voices
tools.verdict: Best-in-class AI voice. Tell listeners when a voice is synthetic.

tools.name: Riverside
tools.pricing: Free (720p, Riverside watermark, 2 one-off hours of separate-track recording); Pro $24/mo billed annually ($288/yr) or $29 monthly; Grow $34/mo billed annually.
tools.best_for: Recording remote interviews in high quality
tools.verdict: Records each guest locally, so remote interviews sound studio-grade. Ideal for interview-driven newsletters.

tools.name: Audacity
tools.pricing: Free and open source.
tools.best_for: Recording and cleaning up voiceovers on a zero budget
tools.verdict: Dated interface but free and capable for simple narration edits.

tools.name: Adobe Podcast
tools.pricing: Free (Enhance Speech: audio only, one file at a time, up to 30 minutes and 500 MB per file, 1 hour a day; Studio: 2 project downloads a day). Since Aug 30, 2026 Adobe no longer sells Podcast Premium on its own: new customers get the premium features through Adobe's Firefly Pro plan (see Adobe for the current price).
tools.pricing_source: official site (podcast.adobe.com/en/features) + Adobe Podcast Premium plan change FAQ (helpx.adobe.com, updated Jul 30, 2026)
tools.best_for: Making laptop-mic recordings sound clean (Enhance Speech), for example a voiceover on a Substack post
tools.verdict: Enhance Speech is impressive on the free tier and enough for reading a weekly post aloud. Premium features (video, bulk uploads, adjustable strength, 4 hours a day) now come bundled in Adobe's broader Firefly Pro plan, so most writers should stick with the free plan.

tools.name: OpusClip
tools.pricing: Free (60 credits/mo); Starter $15/mo (monthly only, 150 credits); Pro $29/mo or $14.50/mo billed annually.
tools.best_for: Turning long videos or podcast episodes into short social clips
tools.verdict: Fast way to get shorts from long recordings. Review the AI's clip choices before posting.

tools.name: Tally
tools.pricing: Free (unlimited forms and submissions, within fair use); Pro $29/mo or $290/yr; Business $89/mo or $890/yr (USD; Tally shows euro prices to EU visitors).
tools.pricing_source: official site (tally.so/pricing; USD amounts from the page's plan data, the visible price depends on your location and monthly/yearly toggle)
tools.best_for: Reader surveys, sponsor inquiry forms and feedback forms
tools.verdict: The most generous free form builder. Substack posts can't host forms directly, so link to it from your post or About page.

tools.name: Datawrapper
tools.pricing: Free (unlimited charts, maps and tables, with a "Created with Datawrapper" credit); Pro $21/user/mo excl. VAT (removes the credit); Business $39/user/mo excl. VAT.
tools.best_for: Clean, accurate charts, maps and tables for data-driven posts
tools.verdict: Newsroom-quality charts for free, and the one chart tool Substack embeds natively: paste the chart's share link into your draft. Interactive on the web and in the app; static in the email version.
tools.notes: Substack's help center documents native Datawrapper embeds (paste the share link into a draft).

tools.name: Flourish
tools.pricing: Free (public publishing with attribution); paid Presenter (via Canva Business) and Publisher/Enterprise plans on contract.
tools.best_for: Animated and interactive charts and scrollytelling
tools.verdict: More dramatic visuals than Datawrapper, but Substack doesn't list Flourish among its supported embeds and pasted embed code doesn't work, so plan on a static image linked to the interactive version.

tools.name: Linktree
tools.pricing: Free; Starter $6/mo billed annually ($8 monthly); Pro $12/mo billed annually ($15 monthly); Premium $30/mo billed annually ($35 monthly).
tools.best_for: A link-in-bio page that points social followers to your Substack
tools.verdict: Fine for bios, but your Substack homepage can often serve as the link. Only pay if you need the analytics.

tools.name: Paved
tools.pricing: Free publisher account, no subscription. Flat-fee scheduled ads need at least 50k subscribers; pay-per-click native ads need at least 1M monthly impressions.
tools.best_for: Established newsletters looking for sponsor demand
tools.verdict: A large newsletter ad network (3,000+ newsletters, per Paved). Its stated minimums of 50k subscribers or 1M monthly impressions rule out most smaller Substacks; start with Hecto or Swapstack until you're there.

tools.name: Hecto
tools.pricing: Free for newsletter creators (no monthly fee); Hecto takes 5% of successful sponsorship sales, plus Stripe's payment fees.
tools.pricing_source: official site (hecto.io/pricing; fee shown as 5%, monthly fee shown as £0)
tools.best_for: Selling sponsorship slots with transparent, upfront prices
tools.verdict: A straightforward sponsorship marketplace: you publish ad packages with upfront prices and a checkout link. Listing is free, but demand varies by niche.

tools.name: Swapstack
tools.pricing: Free for publishers (Swapstack takes 10% on invite-only campaigns from its managed service). Paid publisher plans (Professional $30/mo, Enterprise $200/mo) are listed as coming soon.
tools.best_for: Finding sponsors and affiliate deals for small and mid-sized newsletters
tools.verdict: One of the original newsletter sponsorship marketplaces, with flat-rate sponsorships, pay-per-click and affiliate deals in one place. Worth a free signup to see what matches your niche.

tools.name: Gumroad
tools.pricing: No monthly fee; 10% + $0.50 per transaction on direct sales (profile or direct links); 30% on sales through Gumroad Discover.
tools.best_for: Selling ebooks, templates and guides alongside your newsletter
tools.verdict: The simplest way to sell a digital product to your readers. Fees are high per sale but there's no fixed cost.

tools.name: Ko-fi
tools.pricing: Free to join, no monthly cost. Ko-fi Free: 0% on one-off tips and Goals, 5% on monthly tips, memberships, shop and commissions. Standard: 5% on everything, plus extras like supporter-only content and scheduled posts. PayPal/Stripe fees (usually around 3% + $0.30) apply on top. Ko-fi Gold (0% on everything for a fixed monthly fee) is still offered; price not listed on its page.
tools.pricing_source: official site (help.ko-fi.com: Does Ko-fi take a fee? + ko-fi.com/gold)
tools.best_for: One-off tips from readers who won't commit to a paid subscription
tools.verdict: A low-friction tip jar that complements paid subscriptions. One-off tips are fee-free on Ko-fi Free, but new accounts start in Standard mode (5% on tips), so switch it off in Settings > Payment if tips are all you need.
